_readme: FIAT COUNTY DENS (6 Nov; docs/design/county_stages.md §5): the four County heads' own fights, a plate (744x320) and a wall (744x256) each, 8 jobs at $0.15 (about $1.20).

Out art/fight_boss/<head>_plate.png / _cover.png; the den key reads them by name from the first man. Styled on the zone's first place's pair, palette only (the 6 Nov lesson). ++ --parallel 3. After Matt has read the slice on test art.
Regenerate with python3 tools/make_county_dens_manifest.py; check with python3 tools/art_lint.py.

jobs.description: A first-person view at crouching eye level, as if from behind cover in a light-gun arcade game, looking into a truck stop's back office made into a bailiff's store: hundreds of keys hanging on rows of hooks with no tags on them, wheel clamps stacked on the floor, plain unprinted cardboard boxes of seized goods piled to the ceiling, a battered desk, a strip light, a dark doorway on the left. Nobody in the scene, empty and waiting. No people or figures anywhere. Composed for three figures to stand in later: clear open ground in the middle distance just right of centre, a dark doorway or gap on the left side well down the scene, and room in the right foreground. The ground runs across the lower third; the horizon sits a third of the way down. One continuous scene edge to edge: no repeated sections, no seams. The painting fills the whole canvas right to all four edges: no border, no frame, no margin, no empty space around it. Any signs, boards or fascias are blank, with no lettering on them. The bottom fifth of the scene is plain open ground running to the frame's edge, nothing standing in the foreground: no walls, rubble or cover there, it is drawn over later. Only the palette, light and painting style of the style image - nothing of its view, its place or its subject, which is somewhere else entirely. The painting fills the whole canvas to all four edges, no border, frame or margin. Everything in it plain and unprinted, no lettering, numbers or pictures anywhere. Realistic painted pixel art, soft overcast light, muted cool northern palette, worn and lived-in, post-collapse Britain on a grey day; no black outlines, not anime, not a cartoon, not glossy; no text, no logos.
jobs._where: The Bailiff's own fight, the plate: his den (styled on The Toll Plaza's plate, palette only)

jobs.description: Seen very close from behind, running unbroken across the whole width of the frame: a row of grey steel lockers, their doors dented and some hanging open, no numbers or labels on them, as the cover a player crouches behind in a light-gun arcade game.
